title: Quantum Decision Studio
subtitle: Constrained allocation and variational correlated-electron research.

cases.label: Constrained allocation
cases.title: Optimize the allocation. Keep the constraints.
cases.description: Eight synthetic assets, exactly three holdings, turnover costs and correlated risk. Compare a number-preserving quantum ansatz with exhaustive enumeration and classical local search.

charts.title: Probability on feasible portfolios
charts.xlabel: Lexicographic portfolio index

charts.title: Sensitivity to an explicit uniform-output mixture
charts.xlabel: Mixture fraction (not device error rate)

method: Objective = 4 wᵀΣw − μᵀw + 0.003‖w−w_previous‖₁; equal weights on exactly three of eight assets. Covariance is positive definite by construction.

Depth-2 cost phases alternate with an exact ring-XY mixer in the 56-state feasible sector. Six seeded Nelder–Mead restarts each have a 350-iteration cap. Uniform feasible-state preparation is assumed, not compiled.
Exact enumeration gives A, D, H. Swap local search gives A, D, H, cost -0.038294, after 30 neighbour evaluations. The ansatz is not claimed to outperform either baseline.
limitations: Synthetic forward-looking means/covariance: no historical backtest or investment claim. Small exact simulation is the reference, not evidence of scalability.
Mixer construction and dense exponentiation operate in a constrained subspace; physical preparation, compiled gates and measurement overhead are not benchmarked.
Uniform probability mixing is a sensitivity model, not calibrated gate noise. Both expected objective and success probability must be inspected.

cases.label: Correlated electrons
cases.title: Follow electrons from hopping to localization.
cases.description: A spinful two-site Hubbard dimer isolates the competition between electron hopping and on-site repulsion. A symmetry-preserving variational state is checked against exact and analytic ground-state energies.

charts.title: Ground-state energy across interaction strength
charts.xlabel: U / t

charts.title: Charge localization
charts.xlabel: U / t

method: Construct −t Σσ(c†₀σc₁σ+h.c.) + UΣᵢnᵢ↑nᵢ↓ using fermionic parity signs; restrict to one spin-up and one spin-down electron.
Three real two-level Givens rotations span the four-state real sector. Three seeded BFGS starts minimize the statevector energy for each interaction.
Each result obeys the variational bound and agrees with E₀=(U−√(U²+16t²))/2 within 10⁻⁶ t. Double occupancy is a separate observable, not inferred from a fitted curve.
limitations: This is an effective correlated-electron benchmark, not an ab initio molecule or a battery-material prediction. It is a foundation for extending the battery-design theme.
The ansatz can span this tiny real sector; success does not demonstrate a scalable chemistry algorithm.
Finite-shot evaluation is shown in the Hubbard measurements case. Molecular geometry, basis-set error, device noise and battery voltage are not represented.

cases.label: Hubbard measurements
cases.title: Can sampled observables resolve electron localization?
cases.description: Measure energy, total double occupancy and kinetic energy of the optimized dimer state. Choose a preparation budget and compare equal-shot grouping, independent Pauli terms and energy-focused grouped allocation. The final charts show the energy gain and the precision traded away for other observables. Confidence intervals cover prepared-state expectations; the table exports all three strategies.

charts.title: Energy with conservative 95% CI
charts.xlabel: U / t; 4,096 shots per setting

charts.title: Double Occupancy with conservative 95% CI
charts.xlabel: U / t; 4,096 shots per setting

charts.title: Kinetic Energy with conservative 95% CI
charts.xlabel: U / t; 4,096 shots per setting

method: Independent Born multinomial draws after local Pauli basis rotations; exact-expectation VQE training

Two-sided Hoeffding across independent weighted shots, retaining within-group covariance; marginal 95% CIs for prepared-state expectations. Older group union-bound intervals are retained as a diagnostic baseline.

Preselected D(U/t=6) minus D(U/t=8), using independent preparations at both interactions and a direct two-sided 95% Hoeffding bound. Positive lower bound resolves a decrease; no simultaneous scan coverage is claimed.

Additional count-only equal-tailed Clopper-Pearson intervals for D: one Bernoulli density count when grouped, six Bonferroni-adjusted parity intervals when ungrouped. Contrast subtracts two 97.5% D intervals for at least 95% coverage. No interval selection or intersection; Hoeffding results remain separate. Guarantees assume ideal independent shots and exact sector membership.

All six adjacent density decreases are a fixed family. Separate simultaneous 95% procedures: Hoeffding assigns alpha/6 per difference; binomial assigns alpha/7 per interaction then subtracts adjacent component bounds (ungrouped components divide again across six parities). Shared endpoints are counted once in the seven-interaction preparation cost, and no independence between adjacent differences is assumed. Coverage is per strategy/budget/procedure, not joint across them; no method selection or interval intersection. These new families supplement the unchanged marginal intervals.
Orbital order: 0-up, 0-down, 1-up, 1-down (orbital 0 is least significant bit). Hopping = −(XZXI+YZYI+IXZX+IYZY)/2. D = (2I−ZIII−IZII−IIZI−IIIZ+ZZII+IIZZ)/4. Energy = kinetic + U D, with t=1.
One ZZZZ shot evaluates all density terms together, retaining covariance. Four additional local settings measure hopping parities. Raw 16-outcome counts and seeds are included in results/latest.json.

Equal shots within each strategy; five grouped settings at n shots versus ten independent Pauli terms at n/2 shots, matching total preparations. All observables share those counts. Identity costs no shots. Shot totals exclude exact training evaluations, state-preparation circuit costs, basis-switching overhead and gate compilation. Neither allocation is optimized.

Energy-focused grouped allocation at the same 5n preparations: reserve two shots per setting, then apportion the remainder proportional to (abs(U),1,1,1,1) with largest-remainder rounding. Fixed before sampling; no pilot or exact-state information. Approximately minimizes the relaxed Hoeffding range proxy, not the actual variance. All three observables use these counts; improving energy can worsen density or kinetic precision. Independent seeds 402600+10*i+b. Training and circuit overhead remain excluded.

Ungrouped density uses six independent Pauli means plus the exact identity offset 1/2. Confidence bounds use each coefficient times its measurement range. Exact sampling SD is computed from Born probabilities as a diagnostic; sample SE is estimated from counts. Neither is the confidence-bound half-width.
limitations: Ideal CPU simulation of independent Born shots; no device noise or finite-shot optimization. The exact trained state is held fixed during measurement.

Intervals cover prepared-state expectations, not ansatz bias. Observable plots use marginal bounds; the adjacent-decrease chart separately gives simultaneous scan bounds per strategy and budget. Neither is joint across strategies, budgets or procedures. Sample SE is descriptive, not the CI formula; bounds can extend outside physical ranges.

A small fully expressive Hubbard dimer with t=1; no materials prediction or quantum advantage. Matched preparations exclude circuit and basis-switching costs. Energy-focused allocation uses known coefficient ranges, not exact variances; it can degrade density and kinetic precision.
